paragraphs: Evaluating a language model on a large benchmark can require running hundreds or thousands of prompts. This paper asks whether a smaller, carefully chosen set of tests can provide an accurate estimate of overall performance. The goal is to reduce the computation, money, and time spent acquiring evaluation results while preserving the usefulness of the resulting estimates.

The approach learns dependencies between test examples. Once the model’s outcomes on selected examples are known, those relationships help predict its outcomes on the examples that were not run. Selection therefore matters: the method seeks a subset whose results provide information about the broader benchmark. The authors investigate several selection policies and introduce a reinforcement learning policy that uses the learned dependencies.

The experiments show that this approach substantially reduces the number of prompts needed while maintaining accurate performance estimates relative to previous methods. Its contribution is a way to decide which evaluations to acquire, with predictions supplying the remaining outcomes.
icml-2025-active-evaluation-acquisition-.tldr: A learned selection policy reduces LLM benchmarking costs by testing informative examples and predicting the remaining outcomes.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns a category to each image pixel. This paper studies transferring that ability from labeled source images to a target domain without labels. Self-training can help, but unequal class frequencies and differences between domains can cause the model to predict some classes too often and others too rarely. Those biases also affect the labels it generates for its own training.

Balanced Learning for Domain Adaptation measures this imbalance through distributions of logits, the scores a model produces before converting them into predictions. It identifies over-predicted and under-predicted classes, then aligns their score distributions to shared reference distributions. During self-training, it also estimates these distributions online and adds corrections to the training loss. The resulting cumulative distributions provide structural information shared between source and target domains.

The method does not require advance knowledge of the distribution shift. Across two standard benchmarks, adding it to various existing methods consistently improves segmentation performance, with particularly useful gains for under-predicted classes.
icml-2025-balanced-learning-for-domain-a.tldr: BLDA corrects class prediction biases during domain adaptation, improving segmentation especially for under-predicted classes.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a model to learn successive tasks while retaining what it learned earlier. Its central tension is between stability, which protects existing knowledge, and plasticity, which permits learning new tasks. Gradient projection methods support stability but can constrain plasticity. Combining models offers another route, although earlier merging approaches depend on empirical assumptions and carefully chosen settings.

This paper develops a Bayesian interpretation of model merging for continual learning. From that formulation, the authors derive a closed-form expression for an optimal merging coefficient that adapts to task characteristics. The coefficient controls the combination, so adapting it provides a principled way to adjust how knowledge is merged as the learning problem changes.

BECAME implements these ideas in a two-stage framework combining gradient projection with adaptive merging. Theoretical analysis explains benefits for the stability-plasticity trade-off, and extensive experiments report better performance than the compared continual learning methods and merging strategies. The contribution connects a theoretically motivated merging rule with a practical continual learning framework.
icml-2025-became-bayesian-continual-lear.tldr: BECAME combines gradient projection with Bayesian adaptive model merging to balance retaining old knowledge and learning new tasks.

paragraphs: Chinese scene text retrieval searches for images containing a supplied Chinese text query. Real scenes make this difficult because matching text can run vertically, cross lines, or align only partially. The paper argues that approaches inherited from English scene text retrieval do not adequately address this variety. It introduces DL-CSVTR, a benchmark designed to evaluate retrieval across these different layouts.

The accompanying model, CSTR-CLIP, combines information from the whole image with alignment training at multiple levels of detail. Its two-stage training process addresses two restrictions in earlier approaches: discarding visual features outside cropped text regions and matching text and images at only one granularity. These changes allow the model to use broader visual information while learning correspondences suited to diverse arrangements.

On an existing benchmark, the authors report an accuracy improvement of 18.82% over the previous leading model, together with faster inference. Evaluation on DL-CSVTR also supports stronger performance across layouts. The benchmark and model jointly address both measuring and improving layout-sensitive retrieval.
icml-2025-beyond-cropped-regions-new-ben.tldr: A new Chinese scene text benchmark and CSTR-CLIP model address diverse layouts using global image information and multi-granularity alignment.

paragraphs: LoRA adapts a pretrained model through a low-rank weight update represented by two matrices. Standard practice initializes one matrix to zero, making their initial product zero and preserving the pretrained model at the start of fine-tuning. This paper questions whether that exact starting point is necessary and investigates what happens when both matrices begin with nonzero values.

The authors analyze training dynamics in the infinite-width setting. They find that nonzero initialization makes LoRA more robust to poorly chosen learning rates, especially rates that are too small. Initializing both matrices this way adds random noise to the pretrained weights through their product, but the analysis indicates that this generally does not damage fine-tuning performance.

Experiments across multiple models and datasets support these findings. The result challenges the practical need to begin fine-tuning at exactly the pretrained weights. Its significance concerns sensitivity to learning-rate choices and the tolerance of initial perturbations; the stated findings do not imply that nonzero initialization improves every training configuration.
icml-2025-beyond-zero-initialization-inv.tldr: Initializing both LoRA matrices to nonzero values can improve robustness to suboptimal learning rates without generally harming fine-tuning performance.

paragraphs: Vehicle routing involves choosing routes while satisfying the constraints of a particular problem. Neural routing methods learn heuristics from data, reducing the need to design algorithms manually. Applying one model across multiple routing variants introduces another challenge: it must respond to different constraints. The paper identifies insufficient constraint awareness and exclusive reliance on global connections as weaknesses of existing cross-problem models.

CaDA addresses these issues with a constraint prompt and two complementary attention branches. The prompt represents which routing variant the model is solving. A global attention branch captures information across the graph, while a sparse branch concentrates on selected important connections between nodes. Together, these components provide broad context and focused relational information while making the problem’s constraints explicit.

The authors evaluate CaDA on 16 routing variants and report leading results across all tested variants compared with existing cross-problem solvers. An ablation study finds that each component contributes to performance, supporting the combined design for learning across different routing problems.
icml-2025-cada-cross-problem-routing-sol.tldr: CaDA combines explicit constraint prompts with global and sparse attention to improve neural routing across 16 tested problem variants.

paragraphs: Robotic task planning requires turning a high-level instruction into a long sequence of actions. Language model agents can make planning mistakes and struggle to anticipate later steps. This paper proposes a planner that begins with a draft and repeatedly refines it until it reaches an equilibrium, giving the planning process an explicit mechanism for revising its own output.

A central contribution is showing how to optimize this refinement process end-to-end through an analytical formulation. The planner can be trained with supervised learning without separately curating verifiers or reward models. The authors also introduce a nested equilibrium sequence procedure for closed-loop planning, allowing feedback from the environment or an internal world model to inform the plan.

Evaluation on VirtualHome-Env reports strong performance and improved scaling with computation spent during inference. The findings support iterative refinement as a useful way to spend additional planning computation. The closed-loop component also connects that refinement to feedback, addressing the need to update long action sequences as useful information becomes available.
icml-2025-closed-loop-long-horizon-robot.tldr: An equilibrium-based planner learns to refine long action sequences and incorporate feedback without separately trained verifiers or reward models.

paragraphs: Supervised fine-tuning often combines data from several domains, making the proportions of those domains an important training decision. This paper treats that decision as an optimization problem whose objective is validation loss. It seeks mixture weights that support both overall performance and performance within individual domains, rather than leaving the proportions to manual selection.

The method models how much effective training data transfers between domains and uses fine-tuning scaling laws to describe loss. Small-scale experiments with different mixtures provide the observations needed to fit this model. The fitted parameters then determine optimized mixture weights. Mathematical analysis and empirical results support the approach’s ability to balance performance across the evaluated domains.

In controlled experiments, the optimized mixtures perform comparably to weights found through grid search. Their per-domain losses average just 0.66% above each domain’s best grid-search loss. Reweighting popular fine-tuning datasets also improves validation loss and downstream performance. The authors additionally discuss extending the approach to data selection for domain-specific models.
icml-2025-data-mixing-optimization-for-s.tldr: Small-scale mixture experiments and a fitted loss model yield fine-tuning data weights that perform comparably to grid-search choices.

paragraphs: A sparse Fourier transform recovers a signal using the fact that it contains only a small number of distinct frequencies. Continuous signals are harder to handle than discrete ones because discretization can spread their frequency content, undermining the sparsity that makes recovery efficient. Earlier work offered a fast randomized method, leaving open whether comparable recovery could be approached without randomness.

This paper introduces the first deterministic sublinear-time algorithm for sparse Fourier recovery in the continuous setting. Its stated reconstruction result applies to an on-grid signal with arbitrary noise satisfying a mild condition. Both sample use and running time scale roughly quadratically with the number of frequencies, multiplied by polylogarithmic factors involving the frequency band limit and the gap between frequencies, with additional logarithmic factors suppressed.

The authors characterize the recovery guarantee as optimal among deterministic approaches. That optimality concerns the recovery guarantee, rather than asserting optimal running time. The contribution establishes deterministic recovery under the stated signal and noise conditions, complementing the earlier randomized result.
icml-2025-deterministic-sparse-fourier-t.tldr: A deterministic algorithm achieves sublinear-time continuous sparse Fourier recovery for on-grid signals under a stated noise condition.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether multimodal language models can distinguish beliefs and information associated with different perspectives, an ability examined through Theory of Mind tasks. Existing evaluations largely focus on unimodal systems and judge their outputs without examining internal mechanisms. The authors instead connect behavioral testing with analysis of what happens inside a multimodal model.

They introduce GridToM, a dataset containing varied belief tests and perceptual information from multiple perspectives. Using these tasks, they examine attention heads and find that some can distinguish cognitive information belonging to different perspectives. This internal separation provides evidence of Theory of Mind capabilities in the tested models and offers a mechanism to investigate alongside their answers.

The paper then uses the identified attention-head direction to guide a lightweight intervention that requires no training. The authors report a significant improvement in the model’s exhibited Theory of Mind. The contribution links a new evaluation dataset, an interpretable internal observation, and a targeted method for improving the measured behavior.
icml-2025-from-black-boxes-to-transparen.tldr: GridToM reveals perspective-sensitive attention heads in multimodal models and supports a training-free intervention that improves exhibited Theory of Mind.

paragraphs: Supervised learning commonly predicts labels directly from representations of the input. That arrangement becomes difficult when the labels themselves contain complex information and demand high-fidelity predictions. This paper proposes predictive consistency learning, or PCL, to distribute the challenge of learning that output information across a progressive procedure inspired by generative consistency training.

During learning, PCL receives the usual data input together with a noise-perturbed version of the label as an additional reference. It trains for consistent predictions across different noise levels, connecting input features to label information with varying amounts of corruption. This gives the model a spectrum of label information to learn from instead of relying solely on a direct mapping to the complete target.

The framework also permits multi-step inference resembling gradual denoising, allowing predictions to be progressively refined. Experiments on vision, text, and graph tasks report advantages over conventional supervised training for complex label prediction. The findings support using label structure itself as part of the learning procedure.
icml-2025-generative-modeling-reinvents-.tldr: Predictive consistency learning uses noisy labels and consistency across noise levels to improve complex predictions through progressive learning.

paragraphs: Irregular multivariate time series contain several variables observed at uneven intervals, with measurements that may not line up across variables. Forecasting requires understanding both timing and relationships between variables. Existing approaches can introduce padding that disrupts the original sampling pattern, or use representations that have difficulty connecting observations taken at different times.

HyperIMTS represents the observed values as nodes in a hypergraph. Temporal and variable hyperedges connect these observations, providing a unified structure for passing information along both dimensions. Its message-passing procedure explicitly accounts for irregularity, allowing relationships between variables to depend on timing. This representation works from the original observations rather than requiring padded samples to learn the two kinds of dependencies separately.

Experiments show competitive forecasting performance among leading models while keeping computational cost low. The result supports a representation choice: organizing irregular observations through shared temporal and variable connections can capture useful dependencies efficiently. The stated performance is competitive with existing leading methods, rather than a claim of universal superiority.
icml-2025-hyperimts-hypergraph-neural-ne.tldr: HyperIMTS connects irregular observations through temporal and variable hyperedges to deliver competitive forecasting at low computational cost.

paragraphs: Implicit neural representations depend strongly on architectural choices for their ability to generalize. This paper develops a theoretical basis for choosing input encodings by studying the infinite-width limit. It describes generalization through kernel alignment, connecting the model’s induced relationships between inputs to a kernel designed around prediction error.

The authors first formulate an optimal kernel that minimizes pointwise expected squared error. They then show that adjusting the input feature mapping allows the neural tangent kernel of the encoded network to approximate any positive semidefinite dot-product kernel. This result identifies input encoding as a mathematically motivated means of changing the kernel associated with the full representation system.

The practical proposals are a Kernel Alignment Regularizer, or KAR, and Plug-in Encoding for Aligned Kernels, or PEAK. KAR integrates an alignment objective into existing systems, while PEAK uses learnable input encodings to refine models through that objective. Together, they translate the infinite-width analysis into tools for more principled architecture design.
icml-2025-learning-input-encodings-for-k.tldr: Infinite-width kernel analysis motivates a regularizer and learnable input encodings for principled implicit neural representation design.

paragraphs: This paper asks how to determine whether one variable causes a particular target using observational data when some variables are unobserved. Existing methods that handle these latent variables commonly reconstruct a global causal structure before answering the question. That work can be computationally expensive and redundant when the interest concerns only a specific pair of variables.

The authors introduce local characterizations for several types of causal relationships. These characterizations are necessary and sufficient within the paper’s formulation, allowing the relevant relationship to be identified without first learning the entire global structure. They use these results to construct fully localized algorithms that focus computation on answering the relationship question.

The theoretical contribution establishes soundness and completeness of the proposed approach. Experiments on benchmark networks and real datasets also support its effectiveness and efficiency. The practical significance is that a narrowly targeted causal question can be addressed through local reasoning, avoiding the overhead of global structure learning in the setting studied.
icml-2025-local-identifying-causal-relat.tldr: Local causal characterizations enable sound and complete relationship identification without learning a global causal structure in the studied latent-variable setting.

paragraphs: K-means is widely used for clustering, but reaching a stopping point does not by itself settle whether its solution is locally optimal. This paper examines that distinction. While much existing analysis concerns finding a global optimum, the authors focus on conditions under which ordinary K-means converges to a solution that satisfies local optimality.

Building on those conditions, they propose simple algorithm modifications that guarantee local optimality in both continuous and discrete senses. The modified methods retain the computational complexity of the original algorithm. Their analysis also accommodates general Bregman divergences, extending the treatment beyond the squared Euclidean distance commonly associated with K-means.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that standard K-means can fail to find a locally optimal solution in practice. The proposed methods yield improved locally optimal solutions with lower clustering loss. This strengthens what can be said about the endpoint of clustering while keeping the same complexity class; the guarantees concern local optima and do not establish global optimality.
icml-2025-modified-k-means-algorithm-wit.tldr: Simple K-means modifications guarantee continuous and discrete local optimality while retaining the original algorithm’s computational complexity.

paragraphs: Joint advertising allocates a bundle of two advertisers to an advertising slot. Designing auctions for this setting requires accounting for the bundle structure, which existing mechanisms can overlook when focusing on individual advertisers. This paper studies mechanisms that use that structure to improve allocation and platform revenue.

For a single advertising slot, the authors identify an optimal mechanism. For the more complex multi-slot setting, they introduce BundleNet, a neural network approach built around advertiser bundles. Experiments in the single-slot case show that mechanisms produced by BundleNet approximate the theoretical results. This provides a connection between the learned approach and the setting where the paper supplies an optimal solution.

In multi-slot experiments, BundleNet achieves leading performance and significantly increases platform revenue. The generated mechanisms also maintain approximate dominant strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality, properties concerning truthful participation and participants’ willingness to take part. These approximate properties should be distinguished from exact guarantees, just as the multi-slot empirical results differ from the single-slot optimality result.
icml-2025-optimal-auction-design-in-the-.tldr: The paper derives an optimal single-slot joint advertising mechanism and introduces BundleNet for strong multi-slot revenue with approximate incentive properties.

paragraphs: Visually convincing generated videos do not necessarily depict accurate physics. This paper examines that gap through object freefall, a simple physical behavior that offers a focused test of world modeling. The authors find that leading pretrained video generation models struggle with this task despite producing impressive-looking content.

They investigate whether post-training can improve the behavior. Fine-tuning on a relatively small collection of simulated videos effectively induces dropping behavior in the models. A newly introduced reward modeling procedure improves the results further. The study therefore provides evidence that targeted post-training can change how these models represent a specific physical process.

The findings also reveal limitations in generalization and distribution modeling, so learning to produce dropping behavior does not resolve the broader challenge of accurate world simulation. The authors release a benchmark for evaluating the task, intended as a diagnostic for physical accuracy during video model development. Its value is to make a concrete physical capability measurable alongside visual quality.
icml-2025-pisa-experiments-exploring-phy.tldr: Post-training improves generated freefall behavior, but the study exposes remaining generalization and distribution-modeling limits in video models.

paragraphs: Language models can struggle with reasoning and planning tasks that require exploring multiple possible steps. Chain-of-thought prompting and tree search offer ways to organize this work, but predefined exploration rules can be restrictive, and extensive search can be costly. This paper asks how a model can learn to control the search process itself.

Policy-Guided Tree Search combines reinforcement learning with a tree of possible reasoning paths. A learned policy dynamically chooses whether to expand the current path, create a branch, backtrack, or stop. These decisions determine where additional reasoning effort is spent and when exploration should end, replacing manually specified search heuristics within the framework.

Experiments cover mathematical reasoning, logical deduction, and planning. The authors report better reasoning performance alongside substantially lower computational cost than the compared approaches. The findings support learned search control as a useful component of LLM reasoning: the framework improves both the exploration decisions and the efficiency with which candidate reasoning paths are examined.
icml-2025-policy-guided-tree-search-for-.tldr: PGTS learns when to expand, branch, backtrack, or stop a reasoning search, improving tested reasoning performance while reducing computation.

paragraphs: MuZero-style reinforcement learning has potential beyond games, but real decision-making systems may receive corrupted state information from noisy sensors or malicious attacks. RobustZero targets this vulnerability. It is designed to resist both worst-case and random state perturbations without requiring prior knowledge of how the environment evolves.

The framework trains a self-supervised representation network to produce a consistent initial hidden state despite perturbations. That consistency matters because the hidden state supports the policy: keeping the representation stable helps preserve action choices when the observed state changes through corruption. A dedicated loss function encourages robustness, and an adaptive adjustment mechanism supports model updates that further improve resistance to both kinds of perturbation.

Experiments span classical control, energy systems, transportation, and MuJoCo environments. The results show that RobustZero can outperform leading comparison methods in defending against state perturbations. This supports its use as a robustness-focused extension of MuZero-style learning, with the reported advantage grounded in the evaluated environments.
icml-2025-robustzero-enhancing-muzero-re.tldr: RobustZero improves MuZero-style resistance to random and worst-case state perturbations through stable representations and adaptive training.

paragraphs: SafetyAnalyst addresses two goals for AI moderation: making decisions understandable and allowing safety judgments to reflect particular preferences. Given an AI behavior, it constructs a structured tree of possible harmful and beneficial actions and effects. The tree records affected stakeholders and labels each potential impact by likelihood, severity, and immediacy.

The framework aggregates these effects into a harmfulness score using 28 interpretable weight parameters. Adjusting those parameters provides a way to express different safety preferences within an explicit scoring structure. The authors use this framework to develop an open-source prompt safety classifier, distilling information from 18.5 million harm-benefit features generated by frontier language models across 19,000 prompts.

Across the evaluated benchmarks, SafetyAnalyst achieves an average F1 score of 0.81, compared with averages below 0.72 for existing moderation systems. The findings combine classification performance with a structured account of how potential consequences contribute to a decision. The adjustable aggregation weights are central to the framework’s claimed steerability.
icml-2025-safetyanalyst-interpretable-tr.tldr: SafetyAnalyst scores structured harm-benefit analyses with adjustable, interpretable weights and improves prompt safety classification on evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Representing complex robot actions as discrete skills can make manipulation easier to organize. Existing approaches learn a codebook of skill vectors, but can suffer from codebook collapse and difficulty modeling relationships between skills. STAR addresses both the diversity of the learned skill representations and their composition into coherent behavior.

Its rotation-augmented residual skill quantization mechanism incorporates relative angles between encoder outputs into gradient flow. Depending on gradient direction, points assigned to the same skill code are pushed apart or pulled together. This mechanism is designed to prevent codebook collapse. A separate causal skill transformer models dependencies between skill representations autoregressively, using preceding skill information to support coherent action generation.

The authors evaluate STAR on the LIBERO benchmark and real-world tasks, reporting around 12% improvement over the baselines. The findings support treating skill learning and skill sequencing as connected problems. Maintaining diverse representations provides the skill vocabulary, while explicit dependency modeling helps combine that vocabulary into more complex robot behavior.
icml-2025-star-learning-diverse-robot-sk.tldr: STAR combines rotation-based skill quantization with autoregressive skill composition, reporting around 12% improvement over baselines in robotic tasks.

paragraphs: Optimization-based causal discovery methods can work well on some observational datasets and struggle on others. This paper investigates that variation under nonlinear additive noise models. It separates identifiable problems into strongly and weakly identifiable categories according to how difficult identification is, connecting that difficulty to a characteristic of the causal structural equations.

The authors provide a sufficient condition for distinguishing the categories. They then introduce GENE, a method intended to handle both under the additive noise assumption. GENE searches over variable orders and incorporates conditional independence tests when evaluating those orders. It also restricts the dimensionality of effect variables to ensure scale invariance, a property the authors identify as important for practical use.

Experiments report that GENE is uniquely effective on weakly identifiable problems among the evaluated methods, while remaining competitive on strongly identifiable ones. The contribution explains why identifiability alone may not describe practical difficulty and uses that distinction to guide algorithm design. The stated category condition is sufficient, not claimed to be necessary.
icml-2025-strong-and-weak-identifiabilit.tldr: A distinction between strong and weak causal identifiability motivates GENE, an order-search method effective across both categories under additive noise assumptions.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can generate fluent statements that are unsupported by an image. This paper investigates that behavior by tracking token score rankings during generation. It finds that visually grounded tokens gradually lose favor, meaningful tokens can reach their strongest activation before the final layer, and grounded alternatives can remain highly ranked even when they are not selected.

These observations motivate VISTA, an intervention applied during inference without additional training or external supervision. It combines reinforcement of visual information in activation space with information from earlier layers to promote meaningful decoding. The approach uses relevant information already present inside the model to influence which tokens are ultimately generated.

The authors report an average hallucination reduction of about 40% on the evaluated open-ended generation task. VISTA also consistently outperforms compared methods across four benchmarks, four architectures, and three decoding strategies. These findings support the usefulness of internal visual and early-layer signals for reducing hallucination across the tested configurations.
icml-2025-the-hidden-life-of-tokens-redu.tldr: VISTA steers existing visual and early-layer signals during inference, reducing hallucination by about 40% on the evaluated open-ended generation task.

paragraphs: Federated learning uses communication between participating models as part of training, so reducing the size of transmitted information can improve efficiency. Low-rank decomposition is one approach to reducing this communication burden. This paper examines how to improve its training performance by separating the design problem into three questions: what to decompose, how to decompose it, and how to aggregate the results.

The authors introduce Model Update Decomposition, Block-wise Kronecker Decomposition, and Aggregation-Aware Decomposition to address those respective questions. These techniques are complementary and can be used together. Their organization matters because the choice of decomposed information, its representation, and its eventual aggregation are all parts of the same communication-efficient training process.

The paper supplies a rigorous convergence analysis specifically for Model Update Decomposition. Extensive experiments show faster convergence and higher accuracy than relevant baseline methods. The results support improving several parts of the decomposition pipeline together, while the stated theoretical guarantee applies to the proposed update-decomposition component.
icml-2025-the-panaceas-for-improving-low.tldr: Three complementary decomposition techniques improve communication-efficient federated learning, with faster convergence and higher accuracy in experiments.

paragraphs: Scaling robotic manipulation data is difficult when training examples do not clearly specify the intended task. A policy facing many different tasks can become confused about the target. This paper finds that the robotic data studied is insufficient for learning effective understanding of text instructions, while visual instructions are more comprehensible to the policy.

Vision Instructed Pre-training, or VIP, uses visual information to specify task targets. A straightforward version would predict the actions connecting a current observation to a future image. The authors identify insufficient target detail in a single future image and instead use sparse point flows to supply richer information about the desired progression.

The method is evaluated across tasks in both simulated and real environments. The results show significant performance improvements across diverse tasks, and the resulting policy can perform challenging manipulation such as opening a tightly sealed bottle lid. The contribution emphasizes target specification as an important part of making varied robotic training data useful.
icml-2025-vip-vision-instructed-pre-trai.tldr: VIP uses visual instructions enriched with sparse point flows to clarify manipulation targets and improve performance across diverse robotic tasks.
